tagline: Forest roads pass the remnants of an ironmaking community
intro: Highlands Scenic Byway is a National Forest Scenic Byway in Virginia, listed by FHWA as a 20-mile drive taking one hour before trail stops. FHWA highlights its vegetation, geological formations and remains of a mining community.

Longdale Furnace’s industrial story began in 1827, when John Jordan and John Irvine built Lucy Selina Furnace, named for their wives. William Firmstone and Ario Pardee bought the operation in 1869 and redeveloped it as a hot-blast, coke-fired furnace. Workers’ dwellings and managers’ houses grew beside the operation; the company dissolved in 1914.

At Longdale Furnace, the historic district includes the original stone furnace stack, the company office and laboratory, and two tall brick chimneys. From the Longdale Furnace exit, the Forest Service describes a climb on SR 770 to North Mountain’s trail access at Forest Road 447. Recreation.gov describes a loop returning to Forest Road 447 along North Mountain Road.

moments.title: Lucy Selina Furnace
moments.text: The original stone furnace stack at Longdale dates to 1827. John Jordan and John Irvine named their furnace Lucy Selina after their wives. The business passed to Jordan’s sons before Firmstone and Pardee bought it in 1869. Their redevelopment brought a hot-blast coke-fired operation under the Longdale Iron Company name.

moments.title: The company village
moments.text: Longdale’s district includes workers’ dwellings, managers’ houses and buildings that served the ironmaking operation. The inventory identifies a company laboratory, machine shop and doctor’s office, as well as the two-story company office. Many buildings disappeared after the company dissolved in 1914, but Virginia’s Department of Historic Resources describes surviving traces of the industrial village.

moments.title: North Mountain trailhead
moments.text: At Forest Road 447 and SR 770, North Mountain Trail heads southwest along the mountain with occasional views east and west. The Civilian Conservation Corps built the trail in the 1930s. The Forest Service rates it difficult.

practical: North Mountain trailhead: Snow and ice make the FR 447/SR 770 trailhead difficult to reach in winter. (checked 2026-10-20)
